content.text: Octopuses have three hearts, and two of them stop beating when the animal swims. Their blood is blue because it uses copper-based hemocyanin to carry oxygen. Each of their eight arms holds a large share of their neurons, so the arms can taste, touch, and act with some independence. An octopus can change the color and texture of its skin in a fraction of a second to blend into rocks or coral. They can squeeze through gaps no wider than their beak, which is the only hard part of their body. Most species live only a year or two and die soon after they breed. They are among the most intelligent invertebrates, and some can open jars, solve mazes, and recognize individual people.
